summary: Final MV-2018-336 readout combining plasma binding, bidirectional permeability and DMSO-dilution solubility. The soluble branch retained an efflux liability, so Quorenthel chose to redesign the exposed amine rather than increase lipophilicity.

slides.title: Absorption question and study record
bullets: Separate dissolved availability, directional flux and unbound plasma fraction before recommending chemistry

slides.title: Matrices and conditions
bullets: fu,p by equilibrium dialysis: human plasma, 4 h at 37 °C
Caco-2 flux and efflux ratio: bidirectional transport at 10 µM, pH 7.4
DMSO-dilution solubility: PBS at pH 7.4; kinetic endpoint
slides.notes: Kinetic solubility after DMSO dilution is not thermodynamic solubility or proof of formulation performance.

slides.title: Matrix acceptance: recovery matters
bullets: Helen Marchwood: review dialysis and transport recovery with the assay worksheet
Javier Quintana: evaluate donor, receiver and plasma response in their respective matrices
Inspect monolayer integrity and nonspecific loss before interpreting weak receiver signal

slides.title: Analytical limits on ratios and fractions
bullets: Efflux ratio is B-A Papp divided by A-B Papp; a weak denominator can make the ratio unstable
Very low unbound signal requires the analyte-specific quantitation limit
Neither binding nor solubility alone predicts oral exposure
slides.notes: No numerical acceptance threshold or quantitation limit is added. Recovery columns travel with the corresponding measurements.

slides.title: Bidirectional asymmetry across QP07
slides.notes: Complete referenced test article set, in assay worksheet order; this is not a sorted ranking.

slides.title: QP07 aminopyrazines: structure context
slides.notes: Representative structures aid identity matching; they do not designate nominated leads.

slides.title: Decision after matrix comparison
bullets: High efflux persisted in the otherwise soluble branch
Quorenthel chose to redesign the exposed amine rather than increase lipophilicity
Keep solubility and binding alongside permeability in the next test article set
slides.notes: Transport asymmetry does not identify a specific transporter. No transporter-inhibition experiment is reported.

slides.title: Carry into the next chemistry cycle
bullets: Quorenthel Pharma GmbH: alter exposed-amine presentation and retain the soluble branch as comparator
Megan Larkin: carry directional-flux limitations into the DMPK memo
Repeat combined triage on the revised set; trace the current data through {{PRJ0060:lims_id}}
